'''Innovative learning''' is [[learning]] to anticipate, analyse, and resolve new problems.

== History ==

According to ''[[Source:No Limits to Learning (Book)|Botkin et al.]]'', traditionally, individuals and societies have mostly adopted continuous [[maintenance learning]]. However, '''innovative learning''' was largely ponctual, stimulated by shock from external events, such as natural catastrophes or war.

== Importance ==

Modern academics assign great importance to innovative learning.

=== The modern context ===

As outlined in ''[[Source:No Limits to Learning (Book)|Botkin et al.]]'', human technological capacity is unprecedented. Human beings alive today are capable of impacting themselves and their planet in ways unthoughtof only a few generations before, such as via a drastic, massive nuclear accident, or slow, persisting pollution and contamination of the natural environment. Therefore, the [[human gap]] is now an [[existential risk]] for humanity, to which simply maintaining our current socioeconomical and cultural structures does not constitute an adequate response. Each individual must, through collective learning, be able to understand the modern socioeconomical and environmental challenges facing them, and respond to them via individual action and collective democratic power. <ref>{{#cite:Q2658}}</ref>
